t.4.1: Here has come the season of Hemanta, delightful with crops and the sprouting of new shoots, its lodhra trees in full bloom and its rice fully ripened, its lotuses withered away and its frost falling.
t.4.3: Bracelets and armlets no longer cling to the pairs of arms of the graceful women, nor does fresh silk cling to the orbs of their hips, nor fine, thin cloth to their full, swelling breasts.
t.4.2: The round breasts of amorous, full-bosomed women are not adorned with charming necklaces, pale with the tint of sandal paste and bright like frost, jasmine and the moon.
t.4.5: For the festival of love, women make their limbs anointed with kālīyaka paste, their lotus faces adorned with leaf-patterned designs, and their hair perfumed with the smoke of dark aloewood.
t.4.4: Women do not adorn their hips with girdle-strings bright with gold and gems, nor their lotus-feet, which share the loveliness of lotuses, with anklets that echo the cry of the haṃsa.
t.4.6: Young women, their faces thin and pale from the fatigue of love-play, having attained the fullness of delight, do not laugh aloud, seeing their lower lips bitten by the tips of teeth and smarting with pain.
t.4.8: The tracts of land between the village boundaries, heaped with abundant yields of ripened rice, adorned with herds of does, and resounding with the charming cries of krauñca birds, fill the heart with longing.
t.4.7: Having reached the splendor of the chests of women with full breasts, and grown distressed from being crushed against them, the cold season seems to weep at dawn with the dewdrops that cling to the tips of the grass and fall.
t.4.9: Lakes graced with blue lotuses in full bloom and adorned with impassioned kādamba geese, their waters clear and deliciously cool, captivate the hearts of men.
t.4.11: Beloved, the priyaṅgu vine, coming to ripeness and shaken ceaselessly by winds chilled with the newborn frost, turns pale like a graceful woman parted from her lover.
t.4.10: Having looked upon the road, its waters now wholly dried away, the fawn-eyed women, holding in their hearts their husbands wearied by journeying abroad, and themselves being gazed upon, seem to awaken their cherished longings.
t.4.12: With mouths fragrant from the sweet scent of flower-wine, their limbs perfumed by the breezes of their breath, lying with limbs entwined in one another's, people sleep, pervaded by the flavour of desire.
t.4.13: By lips bearing the wounding marks of teeth, and by breasts inscribed with the tips of fingers, is the merciless enjoyment of love-making betrayed in women in the freshness of their youth.
t.4.14: In the early morning sunshine, some young woman, mirror held fast in her hand, adorns her lotus face; and drawing down her lower lip, its sweetness drunk by her dearest and bitten by the tips of his teeth, she gazes at it.
t.4.15: Another woman, her body weary from the exertion of lovemaking to her heart's content, her lotus eyes reddened from staying awake all night, her loosened mass of hair spilling charmingly and dishevelled over her shoulders, falls asleep, warmed by the gentle rays of the sun.
t.4.16: Other young women, their thick dark tresses flowing to the tips, their slender bodies bowed beneath the weight of full, high breasts, take from their heads the faded garland whose lovely fragrance has been fully enjoyed, and arrange their hair anew.
t.4.18: Other lovely young women, long wearied by the exertion of love's play, their slender bodies grown languid, the regions of their full breasts bristling with thrilled gooseflesh, apply fragrant oil to anoint themselves.
t.4.17: Another woman, joyful as she looks upon her body enjoyed by her beloved, the lovely beauty of her lips freshly adorned, puts on her bodice, her limbs marked with nail-scratches and her eyes half-closed beneath her dark, charming, dangling curls.
t.4.19: Delightful with its many charms, captivating the hearts of women, its village bounds crowded with abundant ripened rice, its frost fallen all around, and sung to by the cries of the krauñca birds, may this season joined with cold bestow happiness upon you.
